task: have or set up a telehealth visit (Teladoc, Amwell, MDLive, Sesame, a health system's video-visit flow): sign in, request or schedule a visit, work through the intake questions, pass the camera/mic tech check, and join the video visit or reach the visit-confirmed or waiting-room state; complete when the in-visit screen or the confirmed-visit state is shown. Surface pinned: the telehealth product's flow — not telehealth-industry commentary, not in-person clinic vlogs. (Booking an in-person appointment belongs to doctor; records belong to patientportal.)

tree.label: Have or set up a telehealth visit
tree.note: 1 to 5 book the visit; 6 to 9 attend it; a visit booked elsewhere starts at 6; 6 runs any time before the appointment, and 6.6 with 6.7 usually fires mid-8 as the meeting app first launches; 7 before 8 where the venue gates the visit on check-in; 8 at the appointed time; 9 once the provider arrives

children.label: Reach the care service
children.note: 1.1 for a fresh booking; 1.2 when the account already exists; 1.3 where a guest run is allowed; 1.4 when several patients share the account; 1.5 before starting anything

questions.question: Is the booking flow actually entered from the service's own start control?
questions.why: The homepage features a prominent 'GET STARTED' button alongside introductory pricing, serving as the primary entry point to initiate a new appointment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the opportunity to review the platform's advertised starting prices and marketing claims before starting the booking flow.
questions.check: Does the page's start/get-started control lead into the actual booking or scheduling flow, rather than an unrelated page or ad?
questions.say_example: entered booking through the service's own start control

questions.question: Are these the correct login credentials for your patient portal account?
questions.why: The screen shows a pre-filled username and password, which must be accurate to successfully access your patient portal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to ensure the agent is logging into your specific health account rather than an incorrect one.
questions.check: What username or email is pre-filled in the sign-in form?
questions.say_example: The sign-in box is pre-filled with <a saved username>. If that's not your account, I'll stop before signing in.

questions.question: Does the page say this email already has an account, and offer signing in instead of registering again?
questions.why: Users often forget they have an existing account with a telehealth platform or health system, and attempting to register again can result in a locked state or split medical records.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might get stuck in an error loop or use an alternate email address, which splits your medical history across multiple disconnected patient profiles.
questions.check: Does the page show a message indicating an account already exists for this email, prompting sign-in or a password reset instead of new registration?
questions.say_example: This email already has an account, so I'm signing in instead of registering again. That keeps your records from splitting.

questions.question: Should I enter my email for a discount, sign in, or close the pop-up?
questions.why: The screen presented a pop-up offering a discount on the first appointment in exchange for an email address, which affects both the cost of the visit and account registration.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide whether to trade their email address for a promotional discount or dismiss the pop-up to continue browsing.
questions.verify_form: The agent hit the discount pop-up - check whether it handed over your email for the 20 percent offer, signed in, or dismissed it; if it typed your email, you were signed up for marketing you never asked for.
questions.check: Does the page show a pop-up offering a discount in exchange for entering an email, with an option to dismiss it?
questions.say_example: There's a pop-up offering <a percent> off for your email. I'll close it without signing you up unless you want the discount.

questions.question: Which patient profile are you scheduling the appointment for?
questions.why: The dashboard asks who needs help today and displays multiple family member profiles alongside an option to add a dependent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent might select the wrong family member's profile for the medical consultation.
questions.check: Does the page show more than one patient profile (e.g., family members) to choose from before booking?
questions.say_example: This account has more than one person on it. Who is this visit for, you or <a family member>?

questions.question: Do you want to look at the COVID-19 resources, or just sign in?
questions.why: The screen displays a COVID-19 alert with informational links for specific medical centers before allowing access to the login page.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to read potentially important COVID-19 updates and resources specific to your medical center.
questions.verify_form: The agent went straight past the service's information banners to the login - check nothing it skipped applied to your situation; it decided for you that none of it mattered.
questions.check: Does the login page show a COVID-19 or public-health banner with links, before login?
questions.say_example: There's a COVID notice on this page with some links. I skipped it to sign in. Say if you want me to check it first.

questions.question: Should you confirm your email before updating your health profile?
questions.why: The dashboard displays a red banner stating your email is unconfirmed and a tooltip indicating an account is not yet active.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to decide whether to verify your contact information before entering personal health details.
questions.verify_form: The agent skipped the account's unconfirmed-email warning - check whether reminders and results can actually reach you; it decided the warning could wait.
questions.check: Does the dashboard show a banner warning that the account email is unconfirmed?
questions.say_example: Your email on this account isn't confirmed, so reminders and results might not reach you. Confirm it now, or keep going?

children.label: Choose the visit kind
children.note: 2.1 where the venue asks; then 2.2; 2.3 where the venue prices insurance against self-pay

questions.question: What kind of care do you need today?
questions.why: The screen asks whether you need urgent care, ongoing care, or are just browsing to route you to the correct scheduling path.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally classify the urgency and nature of your medical needs.
questions.verify_form: The agent picked a care path - check whether it read your need as urgent or ongoing, because everything offered after follows from that reading of your situation.
questions.check: Does the page ask you to choose between care options like urgent, ongoing, or browsing before scheduling?
questions.say_example: This asks whether you need care today, ongoing care, or you're just looking. Which is it? Everything after follows from this.

questions.question: Which type of service do you want to request?
questions.why: The screen requires you to choose between a Medical Visit and a Therapist, both listed at $0, to ensure you are routed to the appropriate provider.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means an agent might select the wrong type of care, such as booking a therapist when you actually need a general medical visit.
questions.check: Does the page require choosing a service type (e.g., a medical visit vs. therapy) before continuing?
questions.say_example: This offers more than one kind of visit, <a medical visit> or <a therapy session>. Which do you want?

questions.question: Which provider do you want for this visit?
questions.why: The screen lists different providers with varying credentials, patient ratings, and out-of-pocket prices for you to evaluate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to personally balance a provider's ratings and credentials against their specific cost.
questions.verify_form: The agent chose a care category and a provider - check who it booked and for what kind of visit; a plausible-looking mismatch here books a real clinician's time for the wrong problem.
questions.check: Does the page list specific providers with differing credentials and prices to choose from?
questions.say_example: There's more than one provider here, with different credentials and prices. Which one do you want to book?

questions.question: Which appointment duration and payment method do you want to select?
questions.why: The screen offers various appointment lengths ranging from 15 to 60 minutes, split between out-of-pocket cash prices and insurance-covered options.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Letting an agent choose could result in paying out-of-pocket for a visit instead of using your insurance, or booking a longer session than you actually need.
questions.verify_form: The agent picked an appointment length and a rate - check whether it chose the insurance price or a cash rate, and how long a session; both change what this costs you.
questions.check: Does the page require choosing an appointment length and whether to pay with insurance or self-pay, with different prices for each combination?
questions.say_example: Sessions run <15 to 60 minutes> and price depends on insurance or self-pay. Which length, and which way do you want to pay?

questions.question: Did the platform flag your insurance as out-of-network or inactive, automatically switching your payment to a high self-pay rate?
questions.why: If insurance verification fails in the background, the system often silently defaults to charging the full cash price to the backup credit card.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might be charged a massive out-of-pocket fee because the agent ignored the insurance rejection and proceeded with the booking.
questions.check: Does the page show a message that your insurance was flagged out-of-network or inactive, with billing switched to a self-pay rate?
questions.say_example: Your insurance came back out-of-network, so this switched to the self-pay rate of <an amount>. Keep going at that price?

questions.question: Do you need to contact the clinic to verify your insurance is accepted before booking?
questions.why: The scheduling instructions explicitly prompt you to contact the clinic to ask if your insurance is accepted before setting up the telehealth appointment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the prompt to verify their insurance coverage directly with the clinic, potentially resulting in an unexpected out-of-network bill for the visit.
questions.verify_form: The agent booked without verifying your coverage with the clinic - check whether the plan was confirmed anywhere; if not, the visit may bill at a rate nobody agreed to.
questions.check: Does the page instruct you to contact the clinic to confirm your insurance is accepted before booking?
questions.say_example: This page says to call the clinic first to confirm your insurance is accepted. Booking alone doesn't confirm it. Want that noted before we continue?

children.label: Pick the provider and time
children.note: 3.1 to narrow the list; 3.2 to weigh who is left; 3.3 where a profile needs vetting; 3.4 decides now against later; then 3.5 and 3.6; 3.7 when nothing offered fits

questions.question: Which filters do you want to apply to narrow down the list of available doctors?
questions.why: The screen shows 144 available providers with filtering options for availability, ratings, credentials, gender, and language.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally prioritize specific provider characteristics like gender, language, or ratings when selecting a doctor.
questions.verify_form: The agent filtered the provider list - check which availability and rating filters it set; those filters silently removed providers you never saw.
questions.check: Does the page apply filters (availability, rating, credentials, gender, language) that reduce the list of providers shown?
questions.say_example: Found <144> providers. Filtered to <the availability and rating you asked for>, which leaves <a smaller number>.

questions.question: Is the provider search page currently toggled to show 'Self-Pay' prices or 'Insurance-Covered' prices?
questions.why: Platforms often use a global visual toggle at the top of the search page that drastically changes the displayed out-of-pocket costs for all providers listed below it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user cannot visually verify which global pricing context is currently active, risking the agent selecting a provider based on a misunderstood or entirely incorrect price.
questions.check: Does the page show a toggle switching all listed prices between self-pay and insurance-covered, and which position is it on?
questions.say_example: Prices on this list are showing <self-pay> rates. Insurance-covered prices would look different. Switch the toggle?

questions.question: Is the doctor you want available, or busy with another patient?
questions.why: The provider list displays real-time statuses, and selecting a doctor who is 'Currently with patient' could result in a significant delay before your visit begins.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might blindly select a preferred doctor without noticing their busy status, causing you to wait indefinitely instead of choosing an available alternative.
questions.check: Does the provider's listing show a real-time status such as available or currently with another patient?
questions.say_example: <A provider> is shown as currently with another patient. Picking them could mean a longer wait before your visit starts.

questions.question: What do this provider's credentials and patient reviews say?
questions.why: Checking the provider's specialties, languages, and specific review scores like bedside manner helps ensure they are a good fit for your medical needs.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to personally evaluate the provider's specific ratings and credentials before committing to an appointment.
questions.verify_form: The agent moved on from the provider's profile - check the credentials and reviews it skimmed past; it judged this stranger good enough to treat you.
questions.check: What specialties, credentials, and review scores does the provider's profile list?
questions.say_example: This provider lists <a specialty> and reviews averaging <a rating>. I'm not judging whether that's a good fit medically. That's yours to weigh.

children.label: Choose now or a scheduled time

questions.question: Do you want to see the first available provider or schedule a specific appointment?
questions.why: The screen offers the choice to either see the first available provider immediately or schedule a visit for a specific time and provider.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select an immediate visit with a random provider when you would have preferred to schedule a specific doctor.
questions.verify_form: The agent chose between the first available provider and scheduling ahead - check which it did; one trades your choice of provider for speed.
questions.check: Does the page offer a choice between the first available provider now or scheduling a specific provider and time?
questions.say_example: You can take the first open provider now, or pick a specific one for later. Which do you want?

questions.question: Which provider and time slot should you select for your consultation?
questions.why: The screen presented multiple providers with different prices and available appointment times.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose a provider and appointment time that best fits their schedule and budget.
questions.verify_form: The agent committed to one provider at one time - check both halves of that line; it spent your appointment on its own reading of cheap and soon.
questions.check: Does the page list multiple providers with different prices and times to choose from?
questions.say_example: There's more than one provider and time here, at different prices. Which do you want?

questions.question: Which appointment type and time slot should you select?
questions.why: The screen requires choosing between a video or phone visit and selecting a specific time slot from the available options to book the appointment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might select an appointment type or time slot that does not fit your schedule or communication preferences.
questions.verify_form: The agent set the visit mode and the hour - check whether it booked video or phone and for when; the wrong mode changes what the visit can even do.
questions.check: Does the page require choosing between a video or phone visit and a specific time slot?
questions.say_example: This visit can be video or phone, at <a time>. Which mode, and which time, do you want?

questions.question: What timezone is the selected appointment time displayed in?
questions.why: Telehealth platforms often display available slots in the provider's timezone or use small, low-contrast text to indicate the timezone, which can easily be overlooked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user might miss their appointment entirely if the agent books a slot assuming local time when the platform is actually displaying a different timezone.
questions.check: What timezone does the selected appointment time display in, and does it match your own timezone?
questions.say_example: This slot shows in <a timezone>, not <your local time>. Converted, that's actually <a different local time>.

questions.question: Do any of the available time slots this week work for you?
questions.why: The calendar showed no availability for most days in the current week, requiring a decision on whether to check the following week's schedule.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to weigh the urgency of your medical needs against the delay of waiting another week for an appointment.
questions.verify_form: The agent judged this week's slots unsuitable and paged forward - check what it passed over; a workable time may have been on the first screen.
questions.check: Does the calendar show no available times this week, prompting a look at the following week?
questions.say_example: Nothing this week works. Look at next week, or does a different day this week actually work for you?

questions.question: If nothing works soon, is there a waitlist you can join?
questions.why: When schedules are full, clinics often provide a secondary option to be notified if an earlier slot opens up rather than forcing you to book months out.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might just book a date months away or abandon the task, missing the opportunity to get you an earlier appointment through the waitlist.
questions.verify_form: The agent did or did not join the cancellation waitlist - check for a waitlist confirmation; joining changes when you might suddenly be expected to show up.
questions.check: Does the page offer a cancellation waitlist option when no near-term slots are available?
questions.say_example: There's a waitlist for earlier openings. Joining means they might call you on short notice. Join it?

children.label: Complete the intake
children.note: 4.1 then 4.2 as the triage asks; 4.3 where free text or a photo is offered; 4.4 and 4.5 to settle the record and the pharmacy - on portal venues the same checks run inside 7 instead

questions.question: Is the chatbot actually using your own employer or plan's benefits?
questions.why: The chatbot introduces itself as the health assistant for a specific sponsor (e.g., Black Car Fund), confirming that your specific organizational benefits are being applied to the visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify that they are using the correct sponsored portal, which could affect whether the visit is covered by their benefits.
questions.check: Does the chatbot identify itself with a specific employer or sponsor name for benefits, and does that match your own?
questions.say_example: This chatbot says it's using <a sponsor name>'s benefits for your visit. Is that actually your employer or plan?

questions.question: Did the intake flag your symptoms as an emergency and send you to in-person or emergency care instead?
questions.why: Telehealth platforms have liability triggers for severe symptoms (like chest pain or shortness of breath) that stop the virtual visit and redirect the patient to an ER or urgent care.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might alter your symptom answers to bypass the block and complete the task, resulting in inappropriate or dangerous medical care.
questions.check: Does the page show the intake flow halted with a message recommending in-person or emergency care instead?
questions.say_example: The intake flagged this as something telehealth can't handle and is pointing you to in-person or emergency care instead.

questions.question: Are your answers to the communicable disease screening correct?
questions.why: The screen asks you to review your responses about symptoms and recent contacts before clicking Submit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to ensure their medical screening answers are accurate before they are finalized.
questions.check: Does the review screen show back the symptom, travel, and exposure answers exactly as you told me to enter them, before submitting?
questions.say_example: Before this submits, it's showing back <the answers you gave>. Does that match what you told me?

questions.question: What symptom and history details does the intake need, and what do you want entered?
questions.why: The intake flow asks for recent travel, existing medical issues, and additional details about your symptoms.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might not know your complete medical history or the specific details of your current symptoms.
questions.check: Does the intake form require symptom, duration, severity, travel, exposure, or medical-history details before it can be submitted?
questions.say_example: This intake needs your own symptom and history details, how long, how bad, any travel or exposure. I can't guess at any of that. What do you want me to enter?

questions.question: Did the triage answers submit and the flow move past the chatbot?
questions.why: The chat interface confirms the information was received and provides a 'CONTINUE' button to move forward.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the reassurance of seeing the confirmation message and manually controlling the transition to the next step.
questions.check: Does the chat interface show the triage answers were received, with a Continue control to proceed?
questions.say_example: recorded the triage answers and moved past the chatbot

questions.question: Is the uploaded photo of your symptom or insurance card actually in focus and legible in the preview thumbnail?
questions.why: The system accepts any valid image file, but the provider needs a clear, well-lit photo to diagnose a condition or bill insurance.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks the provider rejecting the image during the visit, causing delays or out-of-pocket billing, because the agent cannot judge the visual legibility of the upload.
questions.check: Does the uploaded photo's preview thumbnail appear in focus and readable, rather than blurry or dark?
questions.say_example: That photo came out blurry in the preview. Retake it before it's sent to the provider?

questions.question: Do you want to fill out your health history and body measurements, or skip this section?
questions.why: The screen asks for details like allergies, medications, and height and weight, which you can provide for the doctor or choose to leave blank.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide exactly which personal medical details and measurements are shared with the doctor before the visit.
questions.verify_form: The agent filled or skipped the health-history section - check what the profile now holds; a blank history is what your provider will diagnose against.
questions.check: Does the page offer an optional health-history and body-measurements section that can be filled in or skipped?
questions.say_example: There's a health history section, allergies, medications, height and weight. I can't fill that in for you. Do it now, or skip it?

questions.question: Do you want to import your allergy and medication data from HealthKit?
questions.why: The app presented a dialog asking for permission to import your allergy and medication data from HealthKit to help complete the intake process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to control whether your personal health data is automatically shared from your device to the telehealth provider.
questions.verify_form: The agent answered the HealthKit prompt - check whether your phone's health data was poured into this account; that import is a one-tap disclosure of your medical history.
questions.check: Does the page show a prompt asking to import allergy and medication data from HealthKit or a similar health app?
questions.say_example: This wants to pull your allergy and medication history from your phone's health app into this account. Import it, or skip?

questions.question: Is my health profile complete and accurate?
questions.why: The screen prompts you to review your imported allergies, medications, and pre-existing conditions before continuing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify their medical history, which could result in the doctor making decisions based on outdated or incorrect information.
questions.check: Does the page display your health profile (allergies, medications, conditions) for review before continuing?
questions.say_example: Health profile now shows <a medication>, <a condition> on file. That's what goes to the provider unless you tell me otherwise.

questions.question: Did the intake form pre-fill 'None' or 'No' for your medical history, allergies, or medications, and are those defaults actually correct?
questions.why: Many telehealth platforms default to negative responses for medical history to speed up the intake process, requiring manual intervention to report actual conditions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks having an incomplete or inaccurate medical record submitted because the agent blindly accepted the visual default states without verifying them.
questions.check: Does the intake form show 'None' or 'No' pre-filled by default for medical history, allergies, or medications, without you having entered it?
questions.say_example: This defaulted to 'none' for allergies and medications without asking. Is that actually right, or does something need adding?

questions.question: Are your current medications up to date?
questions.why: The screen requires you to verify your existing medications, such as Alprazolam and Ondansetron, and select a preferred pharmacy for any new prescriptions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally ensure your medication list is perfectly accurate and to select the most convenient pharmacy for your current needs.
questions.verify_form: The agent confirmed the medication list and a pharmacy - check both; prescriptions from this visit land at whatever pharmacy it left on file.
questions.check: Does the page list current medications on file and ask you to confirm they're accurate?
questions.say_example: Here are the medications on file, <a medication> and <a medication>. Are those actually up to date?

questions.question: Which pharmacy do you want to use for your prescriptions?
questions.why: The screen requires selecting a pharmacy for potential prescriptions and offers multiple ways to search, such as by zip code, city, or pharmacy name.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to choose their most convenient pharmacy location or preferred delivery method for their medications.
questions.verify_form: The agent set a pharmacy by search - check the branch it picked; your prescription physically goes there.
questions.check: Does the page provide a pharmacy search by zip code, city, or name to select a pharmacy for prescriptions?
questions.say_example: Pick a pharmacy for any prescriptions from this visit. Search by zip, city, or name. Which one?

questions.question: Does the confirmation show the same pharmacy you just picked?
questions.why: The screen displays a confirmation modal with the specific pharmacy name and address to ensure your prescriptions will be sent to the correct location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to verify the exact pharmacy address and ensure it is the most convenient location for your prescriptions.
questions.check: Does the confirmation modal show the same pharmacy name and address that was just selected?
questions.say_example: The confirmation shows <a pharmacy address>. That's different from what was picked a moment ago.

questions.question: Did the pharmacy update actually go through?
questions.why: The screen displayed a success message along with the details of the selected Costco Pharmacy, ensuring any new prescriptions will be sent to the correct location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally confirm that your medications will be routed to your most convenient pharmacy.
questions.check: Does the page show a success message confirming the selected pharmacy was saved to the account?
questions.say_example: No confirmation showed the pharmacy actually saved. It may still be the old one on file.

children.label: Commit the booking
children.note: 5.1 to check the order; 5.2 where a code exists; 5.3 to refuse the upsell; 5.4 for the patient fields, with 5.5 when the form bounces; 5.6 then 5.7 to pay or confirm; 5.8 to 5.10 to prove it landed

questions.question: Are you ready to create a new account to complete this booking?
questions.why: This matters because you must verify the appointment time and out-of-pocket cost before providing your personal information to register.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to review the final price and appointment time before an account is created on their behalf.
questions.verify_form: The agent moved toward checkout with an $89 total on screen - check the appointment line matches what you asked for, and whether it went on to create an account in your name; a new account is a standing identity you may never have wanted.
questions.check: Does completing this checkout require creating a new account, and does the page show the appointment and total to confirm first?
questions.say_example: Finishing this needs a new account under your name. It shows <an appointment time> and <a price>. Before I create it, is that right, and do you want the account?

questions.question: Are the discount amounts consistent across the screens?
questions.why: The banner states a flat $20 savings, which contradicts the earlier Sesame Plus card that promised $20 to $30 off all visits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might ignore the conflicting discount information, causing you to misunderstand the actual savings of the membership.
questions.check: Does the discount amount shown on this screen match the discount promised earlier in the flow?
questions.say_example: Earlier this said <a discount range>, but here it's showing <a flat amount>. Those don't match.

questions.question: Are the held appointment details correct before I complete the booking?
questions.why: The screen displays a pop-up holding your selected appointment time for 10 minutes and requires you to confirm the details to finish booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify the held appointment time and provider before finalizing the booking.
questions.check: Does the hold pop-up show the same appointment date, time, and provider you selected earlier?
questions.say_example: This is holding <a date and time> with <a provider> for <10 minutes>. Does that match what you picked?

questions.question: Do you have a promo code to apply to this booking?
questions.why: The payment details section includes a promo code field that updates the order summary to reflect a discounted total when applied.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might proceed with the standard price, missing the opportunity to save you money with an available discount code.
questions.verify_form: The agent either applied a promo code or paid full price - check the order total; if you had a code and it went unused, the difference is real money.
questions.check: Does the checkout page have a field to enter a promo code before payment?
questions.say_example: no promo code entered

questions.question: Did the order total actually change after the promo code was entered?
questions.why: The system must process the entered promo code and reduce the total price, which confirms the code is valid and the discount has been successfully applied before payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might enter a promo code but fail to verify that the total actually decreased, resulting in you paying the full price if the code was expired or invalid.
questions.check: Does the order total change to reflect the promo code after it's entered?
questions.say_example: The code didn't change the total. It may not have applied.

questions.question: Do you want to upgrade to a paid membership plan for a discount on this visit?
questions.why: The waiting room screen advertises a Sesame Plus membership that offers a $20 discount on the current visit and other future perks.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to decide if the membership's financial benefits are worth the subscription cost based on their personal healthcare needs.
questions.verify_form: The agent answered the membership upsell - check whether a recurring membership was declined or bought alongside your visit; that is a subscription decision, not a booking step.
questions.check: Does the page offer a paid membership upgrade (e.g., a plus membership) alongside a discount on this visit?
questions.say_example: There's a paid membership offer here for <a discount> off. That's an ongoing subscription, not part of booking this visit. Want it, or skip?

questions.question: What is the reason for your appointment and what phone number should be used for notifications?
questions.why: The screen requires the patient's information, the reason for the appointment, and a valid US phone number to complete the booking.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify the exact reason for their visit and ensure their preferred contact information is used for notifications.
questions.check: Does the page require a reason for the appointment and a phone number for notifications?
questions.say_example: This needs a reason for the visit in your words, plus a number for notifications. What do you want me to put for each?

questions.question: Who is this appointment for, and what sex do you select for the patient profile?
questions.why: The platform requires a binary sex selection because some pharmacies do not support other options for prescriptions.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the platform's explanation for why the sex options are limited to male and female.
questions.check: Does the patient-profile form ask who the appointment is for and require a sex selection?
questions.say_example: This needs to know who the visit is for, and a sex option for the profile. Only <binary options> are offered here. What do you want selected?

questions.question: Is a phone number entered yet?
questions.why: The contact information form includes fields for a mobile and home phone, and leaving them blank might trigger an error.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify the best phone number for the provider to reach them if the video connection fails.
questions.check: Does the contact form show a phone number entered in the mobile or home field?
questions.say_example: No phone number is entered yet. This form may block continuing without one.

questions.question: Do you want to opt out of receiving a reminder call for this appointment?
questions.why: The appointment details page includes a specific link to let staff know you don't need a reminder call, which updates your notification preferences for this visit.

questions.question: Do you want to proceed even though the stated deposit wasn't actually collected?
questions.why: The instructions explicitly stated a $50 deposit was required, but the system allowed you to begin the visit without prompting for payment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to clarify the payment discrepancy and might face an unexpected bill or administrative issue later.
questions.verify_form: The instructions named a deposit and the agent proceeded without paying one - check whether money is still owed at the visit; the mismatch is either a fee waived or a surprise bill.
questions.check: Did the instructions state a deposit was required, but the system let you proceed without being charged one?
questions.say_example: The instructions said a deposit was required, but nothing was actually charged before this let you continue. Go ahead, or check whether it's still owed?

questions.question: Is the visit started from the appointment's begin control once check-in completes?
questions.why: The appointment details page confirms your intake information is on file and provides a specific button to launch the video connection.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the visual confirmation that their intake information was successfully submitted and the immediate readiness cue to join the provider.
questions.check: Does the appointment page show a specific control to launch the video connection once check-in is complete?
questions.say_example: started the visit from the appointment's own begin-visit control

questions.question: Are you ready to join the video visit now?
questions.why: The screen indicates that it is time for your appointment and provides a button to begin the video visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally confirm you are present and ready to transition into the live consultation with your doctor.
questions.check: Does the page show it's time for the appointment with an active button to begin the video visit?
questions.say_example: It's time for the visit, and the join button is active. Ready to go in?

questions.question: Is the visit started from the reminder for the correct provider and time, not a different listed appointment?
questions.why: The home page displays a reminder for your upcoming appointment with the specific provider along with a direct button to begin the visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss the chance to verify the provider's name and the exact appointment time before entering the virtual waiting room.
questions.check: Does the reminder's provider and time match the appointment that was booked, especially if more than one appointment is listed?
questions.say_example: This reminder shows <a provider and time>. Check it matches the appointment that was actually booked, not a different one.

questions.question: What should you do when Safari says the address is invalid?
questions.why: The browser displays an 'invalid address' error because the device lacks the Zoom app needed to open the video link.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the context that they must install a separate application to successfully attend their telehealth visit.
questions.check: Does the browser show an invalid-address error because a required app isn't installed to open the video link?
questions.say_example: Safari says this address is invalid. That usually means the required app isn't installed yet. Get it now?

questions.question: Should you join the meeting directly from this generic app screen?
questions.why: The screen prompts for a Meeting ID to join manually, but telehealth visits typically must be launched directly from the patient portal app to connect properly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses their appointment if the agent gets stuck trying to manually enter a meeting ID instead of returning to launch the visit through the health app.
questions.check: Does a generic 'enter Meeting ID' screen appear, separate from the portal's own launch path for this visit?
questions.say_example: This is a generic join screen, not launched from your visit in the portal. Joining here might not connect the same way. Go back and launch it from the portal instead?

questions.question: How do you reconnect if the video call drops?
questions.why: The screen provides specific instructions to return to the OSF MyChart appointment screen to reconnect if you accidentally get disconnected.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user misses the knowledge of how to independently troubleshoot and rejoin their medical appointment if the connection fails.
questions.check: Does the page provide specific instructions for reconnecting if the video call disconnects?
questions.say_example: If the call drops, instructions say to go back to <the appointment screen> to reconnect.

children.label: Let the browser open the app

questions.question: Do you accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy to create your account?
questions.why: The platform requires your agreement to its terms and privacy policy, which explain what data is stored and why, before you can create an account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to review how your personal health data will be stored and used by the platform before granting consent.
questions.verify_form: The agent accepted the video client's terms and privacy policy on your behalf - check what was agreed to; that consent binds you, and nobody read it to you.
questions.check: Does creating the video-client account require accepting Terms of Service and a Privacy Policy?
questions.say_example: Creating this account means agreeing to its terms and privacy policy. Nobody's read those to you yet. OK to accept and continue, or want a summary first?

questions.question: How do you want to handle the blocked popup warning?
questions.why: The browser displayed a "Popup blocked" warning, which must be resolved by allowing popups for this site to open the video test window.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to manage your browser's security preferences and decide whether to permanently allow popups for this specific healthcare site.
questions.check: Does the browser show a blocked-popup warning that must be allowed to open the video test window?
questions.say_example: allowed the pop-up so the video window could open

questions.question: Which site's pop-ups need to be allowed so the video window can open?
questions.why: The Safari Preferences window lists multiple open websites, and you must identify the correct Johns Hopkins domain to grant pop-up permissions to so the visit can launch.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally verify and control which specific medical domains are granted permission to open pop-up windows on your device.
questions.check: Does the browser preferences list multiple open websites, requiring the correct clinic domain to be selected for pop-up permission?
questions.say_example: Multiple sites are listed here, so I'm allowing pop-ups for <the clinic's actual domain>, not the others.

questions.question: How should I handle the browser prompt to open the external video application?
questions.why: The browser prompts to open the VSee application to launch the online clinic video session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over whether to install the required video software or proceed with an existing installation.
questions.check: Does the browser prompt to open an external video app to launch the visit?
questions.say_example: The browser wants to open <the video app> to launch the visit, so I'm allowing it.

questions.question: Which option do you choose to launch the newly installed app?
questions.why: The screen offers both an 'OPEN IN APP' banner and a 'Launch here' text link to transition from the browser to the app.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user's preference for which interface element to interact with when opening the external application.
questions.check: Does the page offer both an 'Open in App' banner and a 'Launch here' link to proceed?
questions.say_example: used the Open in App banner to launch

questions.question: Should the browser remember your choice to always open VSee links automatically?
questions.why: The browser prompt to open the external video application includes a checkbox to 'Remember my choice for VSee links' for future visits.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their browser's security settings regarding whether external medical applications can launch automatically in the future without asking.
questions.verify_form: The browser offered to remember the open-the-app choice - check whether it was remembered; that default fires on every future link of this kind.
questions.check: Does the browser prompt include a checkbox to remember this choice for all future links of this type?
questions.say_example: There's a 'remember my choice' box here. Checking it makes every future link like this open automatically. Check it, or decide each time?

children.label: Choose video and audio to enter

questions.question: Is the webcam turned on for the meeting, and is 'always show this preview' checked?
questions.why: The screen asks whether to join the meeting with your video feed active and provides a toggle to always show this preview dialog in the future.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent decides your initial camera state and future preview settings, potentially broadcasting your video before you are ready.
questions.verify_form: The agent chose whether your camera is live on entry - check the join-with-video choice and the preview toggle; walking in camera-on is a decision about your own room.
questions.check: Does the join screen show a toggle for joining with video on, plus a checkbox to always show this preview in the future?
questions.say_example: This would join with your camera <on or off>, and there's a box to always show this preview next time. Keep that checked, or turn it off?

questions.question: How will you connect your audio for the visit?
questions.why: The screen requires you to select an audio connection method, such as internet audio or dialing in, so you can hear the provider.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to select the most reliable audio connection method for their current network situation.
questions.verify_form: The agent picked the audio route - check it chose internet audio rather than leaving the call silent; the videos call this the step that decides whether anyone hears you.
questions.check: Does the join screen require choosing an audio method, such as internet audio or dial-in, before entering?
questions.say_example: This needs an audio method picked before joining, or the provider won't hear you. Using internet audio.

questions.question: Do you need to use the provided one-tap mobile number to dial into the meeting's audio?
questions.why: The invitation includes a one-tap mobile dial-in number, allowing you to connect to the audio via a standard phone call if your internet audio is unreliable.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses awareness of the dial-in alternative, which could be crucial if they experience internet audio issues during the visit.
questions.check: Does the invitation include a one-tap mobile dial-in number as an audio fallback?
questions.say_example: found <a phone number> available as a one-tap dial-in option

questions.question: Am I in the correct waiting room and is my connection stable?
questions.why: Checking the displayed patient name, appointment time, and connection strength ensures you are in the right place and technically ready for the provider to join.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of personally verifying your connection strength and appointment details right before the doctor appears.
questions.check: Does the waiting room show your name, the correct appointment time, and a connection-strength indicator?
questions.say_example: In the waiting room for <your name and appointment time>, connection showing <a strength level>.

questions.question: What should you do while waiting for the provider?
questions.why: Reviewing the on-screen tips ensures your connection, camera, and physical environment are properly set up for a smooth video visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent cannot physically adjust your camera, find a quiet space, or ensure your local environment is ready for the consultation.
questions.check: Does the waiting room display tips about connection, camera, or environment setup?
questions.say_example: found <a lighting or quiet-space tip> listed among the waiting-room tips

questions.question: What instructions or document uploads are required before entering the waiting room?
questions.why: The waiting room screen specifically asks you to upload your ID, insurance card, and relevant photos before your appointment begins.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to personally review the doctor's specific pre-visit instructions and ensure your sensitive documents are securely uploaded.
questions.check: Does the waiting-room screen list required uploads (ID, insurance card, photos) not yet completed?
questions.say_example: The waiting room is still asking for <an ID or insurance card> to be uploaded. Not done yet.

questions.question: Is this the correct provider's room, and should you enter the waiting room now?
questions.why: The screen displays the provider's name and status, requiring you to click a button to officially enter the waiting room.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally verify they are in the correct provider's room and see the current waitlist status.
questions.check: Does the screen show the provider's name and status with a button to enter the waiting room?
questions.say_example: This is <a provider's> room, ready to enter.

questions.question: Did the room form submit and the waiting room accept the entry?
questions.why: Clicking the green 'Enter Waiting Room' button finalizes the visit form and places you into the virtual queue to see the provider.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate visual confirmation that your intake details were successfully submitted and you are officially in line for the visit.
questions.check: Does clicking Enter Waiting Room result in confirmation of being placed in the queue?
questions.say_example: entered the waiting room queue

questions.question: What rules must I acknowledge before entering the waiting room?
questions.why: The screen outlines crucial safety and privacy guidelines, such as not driving and ensuring a private location, that must be reviewed before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the direct reminder to secure a private location and avoid driving during your upcoming medical conversation.
questions.check: Does the page list safety or privacy guidelines, such as not driving or being in a private location, before entering?
questions.say_example: The page says not to drive and to be somewhere private before this starts. Worth doing now if you haven't already.

questions.question: Is the waiting room showing you're in queue and ready?
questions.why: Verifying your queue position and live video feed confirms that you have successfully reached the waiting room and are ready for the provider.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this to an agent means you are not physically present on the live video feed when the provider connects to start the medical consultation.
questions.check: Does the waiting room show your queue position and a live camera preview confirming you're ready?
questions.say_example: In the queue at position <a number>, camera preview showing you're ready for the provider.

questions.question: Does the waiting room show that the provider is running significantly late, with an option to reschedule?
questions.why: Telehealth doctors frequently run late, and platforms often pop up a delay notification giving the patient the choice to keep waiting or reschedule without penalty.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the choice to reclaim their time and reschedule if the doctor is an hour late, as the agent might just sit in the virtual room indefinitely.
questions.verify_form: A running-late notice with a reschedule offer may be on screen - check whether the agent kept waiting or rescheduled; either answer spends your time without asking.
questions.check: Does the waiting room show a message that the provider is running significantly behind, with an option to keep waiting or reschedule?
questions.say_example: The provider is running <significantly late>, and there's an option to reschedule instead. Keep waiting, or reschedule?

questions.question: How long should you wait in the video room if the provider is late?
questions.why: The appointment details page explicitly instructs you to wait up to 20 minutes past your scheduled time if the provider is not yet in the video.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You miss the clinic's specific policy on provider tardiness, which could cause you to abandon the call prematurely and miss your appointment.
questions.verify_form: The agent is holding in the waiting room - check how long it has waited and what the venue promises; when to give up and call the clinic is your call, not its.
questions.check: Do the appointment instructions state how long to wait past the scheduled time before the provider is considered a no-show?
questions.say_example: Instructions say to wait up to <20 minutes> past the start time. After that, it's on you to call the clinic. I won't decide that for you.

children.label: Attend and wrap up
children.note: 9.1 and 9.2 as the visit runs; 9.3 to leave; 9.4 where the venue holds a checkout; 9.5 for whatever the venue asks after

questions.question: Do you have the provider's permission to record the session?
questions.why: The provider shook his head on the video feed to deny recording permission, prompting the decision to click the 'Leave call' button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally ask for consent and respectfully interpret the provider's non-verbal response.
questions.verify_form: The agent asked or did not ask to record - check whether recording happened and what the provider answered; recording a medical conversation without consent is a serious line.
questions.check: Did the provider grant or deny permission to record the session, e.g., verbally or via a recording-consent prompt?
questions.say_example: The provider hasn't agreed to recording this. I won't record without that. Ask again, or just continue the visit?

questions.question: Is the provider's camera feed visible on the screen, or is it just a black screen with their name?
questions.why: The waiting room might automatically transition to the visit room, but the provider's camera might be off, loading, or blocked, meaning the consultation hasn't truly started.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual confirmation that the provider is physically present and visible on the other end, potentially speaking into a void if the agent assumes the connection is fully established just because the UI state changed.
questions.check: Does the visit screen show the provider's live camera feed, or just their name on a black screen?
questions.say_example: The screen shows <the provider's name> but no live video yet. The visit may not have actually started.

questions.question: Do you need to change your microphone or speaker selection, or test your audio?
questions.why: The menu provides options to select specific hardware like the Internal Microphone or Speakers and test them to ensure your audio works for the visit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to manually verify and test that your preferred physical audio devices are properly connected and functioning.
questions.verify_form: The agent toured the audio-device menu - check which mic and speaker are selected; the wrong device is a silent visit.
questions.check: Does the call menu list specific audio devices to select or test, such as a microphone or speakers?
questions.say_example: audio device menu available if needed: <mic and speaker options>

questions.question: How will you communicate with the provider if your audio or video isn't working?
questions.why: The interface includes a chat button that serves as a text-based fallback if you are unable to see or hear your provider during the session.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally type real-time messages to your provider if technical difficulties disrupt the video feed.
questions.check: Does the call interface include a text-chat option as a fallback if audio or video fails?
questions.say_example: There's a chat option if audio or video stops working. Worth knowing before it happens.

questions.question: How do you turn your video on or off during the visit?
questions.why: The bottom toolbar displays a 'Stop Video' button, which is essential for managing your visual privacy during the live consultation.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to instantly control your own camera feed and physical privacy during the live medical appointment.
questions.check: Does the call toolbar include a button to stop or start your video during the visit?
questions.say_example: video control located in the bottom toolbar

questions.question: Is the visit ended through the leave control rather than by abandoning the page?
questions.why: The screen provides specific instructions to click the 'Leave Visit' button when you are ready to disconnect.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the direct knowledge of how to securely terminate your own private medical consultation.
questions.check: Was the visit ended using the page's Leave Visit control rather than closing or navigating away from the page?
questions.say_example: ended the visit using the Leave Visit button, not by closing the tab

questions.question: Do you need to stay on this page after the video call ends?
questions.why: The screen explicitly instructs you not to leave the page until the consultation is over so you can complete the necessary checkout process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might prematurely close the browser tab once the video disconnects, causing you to miss important post-visit checkout steps or follow-up instructions.
questions.check: Does the page instruct you to remain on it after the call ends to complete a checkout process?
questions.say_example: Stay on this page. It says checkout isn't done until <the checkout screen> finishes, even though the call itself just ended.
